Only :19 (/additional/:id/approve) carries verifyAuth + verifyRoles([1]). servana_api-main/src/controllers/additional.controller.ts:6-8 — `const { userId } = req.params; ... additionalService.createRequest(bookingId, items, userId)`; :26 — `additionalService.generatePayment(Number(req.params.id))`; :63 — `additionalService.getByBooking(Number(req.params.bookingId))`. servana_api-main/src/services/additional.service.ts:11-58 createRequest checks only that the booking exists (:13-18) and then INSERTs with `requested_by = userId` (:26-32) plus caller-supplied unitPrice and quantity (:34-49) — the price is trusted from the request body, not the catalog. :70-97 generatePayment fetches the request by id with no ownership predicate, calls createPayment, then looks up the booking's real customer via getUserInfoByBookingId and emails them the checkout URL (:80-92). :194-203 getByBooking is `SELECT * FROM booking_additional_requests WHERE booking_id = $1` with no scoping. Authenticated successors already exist: provider.routes.ts:73-75 (/worker/additional-work/:id/decision|withdraw|confirm-proceed, verifyAuth) and :166 (/provider/additional-requests, verifyAuth). No caller found for /api/additional/* in servana_client-main/lib, ServanaWorker/lib, or servana_adminportal/src.
findings.recommendation: Put verifyAuth on all six and derive identity from the token, not the URL: drop the :userId segment from createRequest and use (req as any).user.uid, and gate every one of them on assertBookingAccess(bookingId, uid) (servana_api-main/src/services/bookingAccessService.ts:101) — for the :id routes, resolve booking_id from booking_additional_requests first. Also stop trusting item.unitPrice from the body (additional.service.ts:36) and price from the catalog. UNVERIFIED whether the provider web portal calls the legacy paths; that repo is not local, but it is §1-editable so no protected release is at stake either way.

findings.title: Provider live-location response nests the GPS doc under `location`; the client only accepts it at the root or under `data` — the tracking map's provider pin is null on every fetch
findings.hardRule: §9 no duplicate reality / §3 backend canonical / §20 no ghost success
findings.evidence:
The customer's live-tracking provider marker can never render. Envelope names diverge and nothing bridges them.

- Backend: servana_api-main/src/controllers/technicianController.ts:177-180 returns `{ success: true, location: toCamel(location) }` for GET /api/workers/location/:uid. The Mongo doc itself is `{uid, is_online, loc, updatedAt}` (src/services/technicianService.ts:376-391), so after toCamel the GeoJSON point sits at `location.loc`.
- Client: servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/data/tracking_data_source.dart:35-38 unwraps only `result['data']`, otherwise passes the whole envelope; servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot.dart:47-51 then does `raw = map['loc'] != null ? map : (map['data'] ?? map)` and `if (loc == null) return null`. `map['loc']` is null (the key is `location`), `map['data']` is null, so `raw['loc']` is null and fromApiMap returns null unconditionally.
- No bridge exists: grep of servana_api-main/src/utils/fieldParity.ts finds no group whose canonical or alias set contains `loc` or `location`, so applyContextSafeParity in src/middleware/parityMiddleware.ts cannot synthesise the key.
- Blast radius: servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/data/tracking_repository.dart:42-71 assigns that null to `providerLocation` on BookingTrackingState (:94). Both the parallel fetch and the late-uid refetch use the same data source, so there is no path that produces a position.
- The suite certifies the fiction: servana_client-main/test/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot_test.dart:9,37,65 all build fixtures with `'loc'` at the root — an envelope the backend has never sent. Same failure mode as first-pass SC-017, where a green contract test pinned an unserved URL.
- Not previously reported: grep over servana_client-main/docs/ for GeoPositionSnapshot, getProviderLocation, `workers/location` and provider-location returns zero hits across all six first-pass reports.
findings.recommendation: Backend-only and additive, no protected release (§2). In servana_api-main/src/controllers/technicianController.ts:177-180 spread the camel-cased doc alongside the existing wrapper — `res.json({ success: true, location: doc, ...doc })` — so `loc`, `uid`, `isOnline` and `updatedAt` also appear at the root where geo_position_snapshot.dart:47 already looks. Keep the `location` key so any other consumer is unaffected (§4). Then fix servana_client-main/test/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot_test.dart to feed the real `{success, location:{...}}` envelope, otherwise the suite will keep certifying the break. Consider registering a parity group `loc → [location, position, geo]` so the two names converge for future readers.
findings.summary: GET /api/workers/location/:uid returns the GPS doc under `location`, but GeoPositionSnapshot.fromApiMap only reads `loc` at the root or under `data`, so the client's provider-location parse returns null on every call and the live-tracking map never shows a provider pin.

findings.title: The authenticated successor route repeats the same `location` wrapper, so the worker-route migration cannot be completed without a protected client release
findings.evidence: a85998e added GET /api/booking/:bookingId/provider-location as the booking-scoped, authenticated replacement for the unauthenticated legacy lookup, with a documented retirement plan (servana_api-main/src/controllers/providerLocationAccessController.ts:27-29 and docs/WORKER_ROUTE_MIGRATION.md). But the successor was given the same envelope as the route it replaces: providerLocationAccessController.ts:75, :82 and :85 all return `{success, assigned, location}`. Since servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot.dart:47-51 cannot parse a `location` wrapper (see SW2-01), pointing the client at the safe route would change nothing functionally and would still need a client-side parser change to work at all. The migration therefore cannot reach 'legacy traffic is zero' through a backend-only change, which is what legacyRouteTelemetry (src/routes/technician.routes.ts:15) was added to measure. Also note the successor introduces a third state the current client has no representation for — `{assigned:false, location:null}` versus `{assigned:true, location:null}` — which BookingTrackingState collapses to the same null (tracking_repository.dart:94).
findings.recommendation: Apply the same root-level spread to providerLocationAccessController.ts:85 that SW2-01 recommends for the legacy handler, so both routes emit an identical, client-parseable body and the client can be repointed by URL alone at a future scheduled release. Keep `assigned` as an additive top-level flag. Until then, record in docs/WORKER_ROUTE_MIGRATION.md that step 4 is blocked on a customer-mobile release, rather than on telemetry.
findings.summary: GET /api/booking/:bookingId/provider-location uses the same unparseable `location` wrapper as the legacy route it is meant to replace, so migrating the customer app off the unauthenticated route requires a protected mobile release the migration plan assumes it can avoid.

findings.title: `formatBooking` is applied to booking_tracking rows, fabricating `bookingCode: "SVN-undefined"` on the customer tracking response
findings.hardRule: §3 backend canonical / SWEEP formatter rule (command_servana_seo.md step 2)
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/controllers/bookingController.ts:161 returns `{ success: true, tracking: formatBookings(tracking) }`, but bookingService.getTracking (src/services/bookingService.ts:386-396) selects only `status, note, created_at` from booking_tracking — these are not bookings and carry no `id`. In formatBooking (bookingService.ts:494-521), `bookingPk = c.id ?? raw.id` is therefore undefined. The `bookingId` spread is guarded (`bookingPk !== undefined`, :507) but `bookingCode` at :508 is unconditional: `c.bookingCode ?? \`SVN-${String(bookingPk).padStart(6,'0')}\`` evaluates to the literal string "SVN-undefined" on every tracking row. `statusLower` (:518) is likewise stamped onto a tracking event as if it were a booking status. This violates the SWEEP formatter rule, which scopes booking formatters to booking entities. Impact is limited today because the only consumers — servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/data/booking_repository.dart:93-102 (getTimeline) and lib/modules/aircon_booking/data/aircon_booking_store.dart:527-540 — return the raw maps and have no rendering call site in lib/, so the fabricated code is not currently shown to a customer.
findings.recommendation: In servana_api-main/src/controllers/bookingController.ts:161 stop reusing the booking formatter for tracking rows — return `tracking.map(toCamel)`, or add a dedicated `formatTrackingEvent`. Defensively, guard line 508 the same way line 507 is guarded so `bookingCode` is omitted rather than fabricated when there is no PK. Purely additive removal of a bogus field; no client reads it.
findings.summary: The customer tracking endpoint runs booking_tracking rows through formatBooking, which unconditionally synthesises a booking code from an undefined primary key and emits the literal string "SVN-undefined" on every tracking event.

findings.title: Provider-profile projection drops `email`, removing the last name fallback on the booking detail screen
findings.hardRule: §58 privacy (the removal is correct) / §4 (the client-visible delta is new)
findings.evidence: servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/presentation/screens/booking_detail_screen.dart:294-296 resolves the assigned provider's display name as `composed (firstName + lastName)` → `w['name']` → `w['email']` → the literal 'Technician'. Before 65b4337 the raw profile carried `email`, so a provider row with blank name fields still surfaced something identifying. `email` is now explicitly in WITHHELD_FROM_OTHERS (servana_api-main/src/services/providerProfileProjection.ts:84) and absent from PUBLIC_FIELDS (:32-45), so for a customer audience that rung of the fallback chain is dead and such a booking now reads 'Technician'. Withholding the provider's email from customers is the right call under §58 — this is recorded so the behavioural delta is not later mistaken for a parity bug, and because it is a genuine, new consequence of a fix that landed after the first pass.
findings.recommendation: No backend change; do not re-add email. If a display name is wanted for name-blank providers, the correct fix is the one already recommended under first-pass SC-083: return `worker_name` inline on the booking read model (join user_credentials on bookings.worker_uid in servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:209-225) and register a `workerName → [worker_name, providerName, provider_name]` parity group. That also removes the extra round-trip booking_detail_screen.dart:287 makes purely to learn a name.
findings.summary: 65b4337 correctly withholds the provider's email from customers, which as a side effect kills the third rung of the client's provider-name fallback chain, so a provider with blank name fields now displays as 'Technician'.

findings.title: Linked guest bookings appear in the customer's list but 403 on tap — 880d5bc fixed the query and left the access check behind
findings.hardRule: §8 guest customer / §9 no duplicate reality / §11 fail closed
findings.evidence: Two code paths now disagree about who owns a linked guest booking. The list path accepts the link: servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:365-372 returns rows where `b.guest_customer_id IN (SELECT gc.guest_customer_id FROM guest_customers gc WHERE gc.linked_customer_uid = $1)`. The access path does not: servana_api-main/src/services/bookingAccessService.ts:66-75 reads only `SELECT user_id FROM bookings WHERE id = $1` and grants 'customer' solely on `ownerUid === actorUid`; it never queries guest_customers. The backend's own comment at bookingAccessService.ts:53-57 confirms guest bookings have no user_id. So GET /api/users/:userId/bookings returns the row, servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/data/booking_repository.dart:24-36 maps it into the list, and opening it calls GET /api/:id → assertBookingAccess (servana_api-main/src/controllers/bookingController.ts:92) → 403 BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED. The client surfaces that as a bare refresh failure (booking_detail_screen.dart:275-278, 'Could not refresh. Tap ↻ to retry.') with no explanation and infinite retry. First-pass SC-039 described this split under the old phone-matching mechanism; 880d5bc replaced the mechanism — and turned a query that crashed into one that succeeds — without touching the sibling check.
findings.recommendation: Extend resolveBookingAccess in servana_api-main/src/services/bookingAccessService.ts:66-75 with the same linkage the list query uses: after the user_id check, `SELECT 1 FROM guest_customers gc JOIN bookings b ON b.guest_customer_id = gc.guest_customer_id WHERE b.id = $1 AND gc.linked_customer_uid = $2` and return 'customer' on a hit. Use the audited link column only (linked_customer_uid, set at adminGuestService.ts alongside linked_at/linked_by_admin_uid) — never phone. Backend-only, no protected release. Add an authorization test that a linked guest booking is readable by the linked customer and a non-linked one is not, so list and detail cannot drift apart again.
findings.summary: 880d5bc made the bookings list correctly surface admin-linked guest bookings, but resolveBookingAccess still authorises only on bookings.user_id, so every one of those bookings returns 403 the moment the customer taps it.
findings.round2Title: 880d5bc fixed the guest booking LIST predicate but not the matching ACCESS predicate — linked guest bookings still 403 the instant the customer taps them
findings.round2Evidence: List side (fixed): servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:365-372 — `WHERE (b.user_id = $1 OR b.guest_customer_id IN (SELECT gc.guest_customer_id FROM guest_customers gc WHERE gc.linked_customer_uid = $1))`. Access side (unchanged): src/services/bookingAccessService.ts:66-91 — the only customer predicate is `SELECT user_id FROM bookings WHERE id = $1` then `if (ownerUid && ownerUid === actorUid) return 'customer'` (:74-75). A grep for `linked_customer_uid` across src/ returns hits only in bookingService.ts:353,370 and adminGuestService.ts — never in bookingAccessService.ts. Its own docstring at bookingAccessService.ts:53-57 still asserts guests 'cannot reach these routes at all', which is now stale relative to the link the list honours. Consequence for the client: lib/modules/bookings/data/booking_repository.dart lists via servana_api_client.dart:328-334, then tapping routes to `GET /api/:bookingId` (servana_api_client.dart:387-391 → booking.routes.ts:37 → bookingController.ts:92 assertBookingAccess) → 403 BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED. The same 403 blocks cancel, tracking (booking.routes.ts:38), chat (chat.controller.ts:44 resolveAccessForBooking) and PayMongo (paymentController.ts:80).

findings.title: Parity registry mirrors remain two groups behind the backend and there is still no CI check
findings.evidence: First-pass SC-085, re-measured and unchanged. servana_api-main/src/utils/fieldParity.ts declares 58 groups; servana_adminportal/src/app/shared/utils/servana-field-parity.util.ts and Servana.com.ph/src/app/core/utils/servana-field-parity.util.ts declare 56 each. Diffing the extracted canonical-name lists (backend vs admin mirror) yields exactly two names present only in the backend — `email` and `token` — and none present only in the mirror. Drift has not widened across the nine backend commits, but no automated guard was added either, so the next registry edit can silently widen it. Customer-mobile exposure is indirect: ServanaClient relies on the backend response middleware rather than the Angular interceptors, but servana_client-main/lib/modules/profile/data/profile_repository.dart:62 depends on the `email → emailAddress → email_address` alias set that the backend middleware injects, so the group is load-bearing for the customer app even though only the mirrors are missing it.
findings.recommendation: Copy the `token` and `email` groups from servana_api-main/src/utils/fieldParity.ts:36-47 into both mirror files, then run `npx tsc --noEmit` in all three repos (§60). Fold this into the same edit as the totalAmount alias above. Add a CI meta-test that extracts the canonical-name list from all three files and fails on any difference — the first pass flagged this drift as silent, and it is still silent.
findings.summary: The two Angular parity-registry mirrors still omit the backend's `email` and `token` groups (58 vs 56), and no automated check yet exists to stop the next edit from widening the gap.

findings.title: ServanaClient @4868aca cannot be built from a clean checkout — main.dart imports a file that is no longer tracked
findings.summary: The credential-scrub commits untracked the Firebase CLIENT configuration and left only `.example` templates. Firebase client config is not a secret, so this bought no security — but `lib/main.dart` still imports the deleted file and the Android Gradle Google Services plugin still requires `google-services.json`. A fresh clone, and therefore CI and any release build, fails at compile time.
findings.evidence: servana_client-main/lib/main.dart:14 — `import 'package:client/firebase_options.dart';`. `git ls-files | grep -i "firebase_options|google-services|GoogleService-Info"` in servana_client-main returns only `android/app/google-services.json.example`, `ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist.example`, `lib/firebase_options.dart.example`. The real files exist on this machine but are untracked (`ls -la` shows lib/firebase_options.dart, android/app/google-services.json, ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist all present, none in git ls-files). `git diff --stat bab66e4..4868aca` shows `lib/firebase_options.dart | 68 -` deleted and `lib/firebase_options.dart.example | 42 +` added, plus the two platform files renamed to `.example`. The working tree therefore builds and a clean clone does not — the failure is invisible to whoever made the change.
findings.recommendation: Re-track all three files (`git add -f`), since Firebase client config is public by design — it ships inside every APK/IPA. If a policy of templating them is kept anyway, then CI must materialise them from a secret before `flutter build`, and that step must exist and be proven green before the next release is cut (§60). Right now neither is true.

findings.title: confirmOtp is the one route that got assertBookingAccess without sendBookingAccessError — a 403 collapses to 400 and the OTP screen renders 'You do not have access to this booking' as an OTP error
findings.summary: 52667b3 added the authorization call to five handlers and the error mapper to four of them. confirmOtp was missed, so an access denial leaves the handler through the generic catch as HTTP 400 with the access message in the body. The client cannot distinguish 'wrong code' from 'not your booking', and shows the authorization text on the code-entry field with no recovery path.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/controllers/bookingController.ts:71 calls `assertBookingAccess`, but the catch at :76-78 is `return res.status(400).json({ success:false, message: e.message })` — no `sendBookingAccessError`. Compare the siblings that do have it: getBooking :102, getTracking :163, and in paymentController.ts gcashSubmit :24, approve :60, markCashPaid :72, createPaymongoPayment :90. `BookingAccessError.message` is 'You do not have access to this booking' (bookingAccessService.ts:108) and its statusCode 403 (:109) is discarded. Client: servana_client-main/lib/common/presentation/screens/booking_otp_screen.dart:113-115 catches ServanaApiException and calls `_messageFrom(e)` (:163-173), which decodes `message` and renders it verbatim under the OTP input; the fallback would otherwise be 'Invalid code. Please try again.' Either way the screen offers only Resend, which hits a route that does not exist (see the resend-otp finding).
findings.recommendation: Add `if (sendBookingAccessError(res, e)) return;` as the first line of the confirmOtp catch, matching the other six handlers. One line, backend-only.

findings.title: The typed booking-error layer is dead code — BookingErrorMapper and BookingSubmissionResult have zero production call sites, so the now-reachable 401 on POST /api/bookings has no categorised recovery
findings.summary: The client ships a complete error taxonomy for booking creation — including an `authenticationRequired` category — and never uses it. The booking stores instead surface the backend's raw `message`, or the raw Dart exception text for anything that is not a ServanaApiException. 52667b3 made 401 a live outcome of booking creation for the first time, and it lands on this unhandled path: the customer sees the backend string while the global 401 hook simultaneously expires their session and the router bounces them to /welcome, with no explanation and no resume.
findings.evidence: servana_client-main/lib/common/domain/booking/booking_submission_result.dart:63-75 defines BookingErrorCategory (including `authenticationRequired`, `duplicateSubmission`, `networkUnavailable`) and :78-140 defines BookingErrorMapper.fromException (401/403 branch at :127-134). A repo-wide grep for `BookingErrorMapper|BookingSubmissionResult` across lib/ and test/ returns hits ONLY in the defining file and in test/domain/booking_error_test.dart:6-55 — no production caller. What actually runs: lib/modules/aircon_booking/data/aircon_booking_store.dart:456-467 `catch (e) { submissionError = _errorMsg(e); ... }`, where `_errorMsg` (:576-588) returns the decoded backend `message` or, for any non-API error, `e.toString()` — raw exception text on the UI (§21). Same shape in lib/modules/bw_booking/data/bw_booking_store.dart. The 401 body it renders is either `{success:false, code:'UNAUTHENTICATED', message:'Authentication is required'}` (servana_api-main/src/controllers/bookingController.ts:24-28) or `{status:'failed', code:'TOKEN_EXPIRED', message:'Session expired. Please log in again.'}` (src/middleware/verifyAuth.ts:41-45). In parallel, servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:59 fires `onUnauthorized`, wired at lib/common/injectors/main_injector.dart:150-154 to `AuthStateService.update(AuthStatus.expired)` + `SessionService.deleteSession()`, and lib/common/presentation/routes/main_router.dart:144-149 redirects any protected location to WelcomeScreen on `!isAuthenticated`. Also note the analytics event is hardcoded to `FailureCodeValues.networkError` (aircon_booking_store.dart:459-462) regardless of the real cause, so this failure mode is invisible in telemetry too.
findings.recommendation: Route the booking stores' catch through `BookingErrorMapper.fromException` and hold the result as a `BookingSubmissionResult`, so `authenticationRequired` gets a distinct 'Please sign in again — your booking details are saved' presentation and `e.toString()` never reaches the UI. Give `AuthStatus.expired` its own router branch (main_router.dart:144) instead of collapsing it into the unauthenticated redirect, and report the mapped category in BookingFailedEvent. Client-side; folds into the next scheduled release.

findings.title: The first-pass remediation record is wrong — five findings are annotated 'FIXED in <commit>' but are demonstrably still open, three of them client-side fixes a backend commit could not have made
findings.summary: docs/audit/STITCH_CLIENT.md carries FIXED annotations that do not correspond to code. Two of the P0s (SC-001, SC-002) really were fixed and are correctly marked. But SC-035, SC-040, SC-042, SC-043 and SC-091 are all marked FIXED and none of them are. SC-091 is a Flutter widget attributed to a backend commit, and no lib/ file changed at all between the two passes. Anyone triaging from this document will believe the notification and cancellation chains are closed.
findings.evidence: Annotations: servana_client-main/docs/audit/STITCH_CLIENT.md:207 (SC-035 '**FIXED** in bd8c355'), :282 (SC-040, bd8c355), :311 (SC-042, 6d78313), :324 (SC-043, bd8c355), :414 (SC-091, bd8c355). Refutations, all on current code: SC-035/SC-040 — one createCustomerNotification call site repo-wide (bookingController.ts:38), customerCancelBooking notifies nobody (bookingService.ts:565-585); SC-042 — the webhook paid branch (paymentService.ts:421-513) sends an email and no notification; SC-043 — customer cancel still writes `booking_timeline_events` (bookingService.ts:576-585) while `getTracking` still selects only from `booking_tracking` (bookingService.ts:386-394); SC-091 — servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/presentation/widgets/booking_cancellation_sheet.dart:79-91 still has the bare `catch (e)` setting the fixed string 'Cancellation is not available at this time...' and still carries the stale 'BACKEND_GAP-C15-001: no customer-facing cancel endpoint' comment. Decisive: `git diff --stat bab66e4..4868aca` in servana_client-main shows the only lib/ change in the whole range is the deletion of lib/firebase_options.dart — no client fix shipped, so no client finding can be FIXED.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the FIXED annotations from actual code evidence rather than commit adjacency (docs/audit/_generate.py + _findings.json are the source). A fix marker must cite the line that changed. Until then treat every FIXED marker in these six documents as unverified — SC-001 and SC-002 are the only two I confirmed by reading the code.

findings.title: The authenticated successor routes have zero adopters in either mobile app, so the legacy-retirement gate can never be met and customer tracking still rides an unauthenticated route
findings.summary: a85958e added `GET /worker/schedule` and `GET /booking/:bookingId/provider-location` as authenticated, subject-from-token successors, and documented retirement of the legacy family as gated on legacy traffic reaching zero. Nothing calls the successors. The customer app's live tracking still calls the legacy unauthenticated worker-location route, so legacy traffic can never reach zero without a protected release of both apps.
findings.evidence: Successors: servana_api-main/src/routes/provider.routes.ts:177-178, both behind verifyAuth, handlers at src/controllers/providerLocationAccessController.ts (booking id resolved, assertBookingAccess at :69 before the worker uid is resolved at :71). Adopters: `grep -rn "provider-location|worker/schedule" lib/ --include=*.dart` returns zero hits in servana_client-main AND zero in ServanaWorker. What the customer app actually calls: servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/data/tracking_data_source.dart:33 → servana_api_client.dart:350-354 → `GET /api/workers/location/:uid`, which is registered with no auth at servana_api-main/src/routes/technician.routes.ts:37. The client's own comment at tracking_data_source.dart:22-27 states the endpoint is unauthenticated and that the backend ignores the bearer header it sends. Telemetry to measure the legacy family was added (technician.routes.ts:15 `router.use("/workers", legacyRouteTelemetry)`), so the counter will keep reporting live customer traffic indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Either sequence the successor adoption into the next scheduled ServanaClient/ServanaWorker releases (no unscheduled release — the legacy routes keep working meanwhile, §2), or accept that `/api/workers/location/:uid` cannot be retired and instead scope it server-side: require a bearer token and return a location only when the caller holds an active booking with that worker, reusing the exact logic in providerLocationAccessController.ts:60-85. The second option needs no client change and closes the hole now.

findings.title: Payment settlement is not idempotent — approve and mark-cash-paid re-fire the provider's 'Payment Received' notification and reset paid_at on every retry
findings.summary: 6d78313 correctly restricted who may settle, but the settle itself has no state guard. A provider double-tapping Mark as paid, or ServanaWorker retrying after a timeout, rewrites paid_at and sends a second earnings notification for money that arrived once. The first pass noted the notification as an impact of the P0; the replay behaviour survives the P0's closure.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/services/paymentService.ts:76-83 — `UPDATE payments SET status='PAID', paid_at=NOW() WHERE booking_id=$1 RETURNING *`: no `AND status <> 'PAID'`, no version check. Same shape in markCashPaid at :110-118 (which additionally rewrites `method='CASH'`, so a retry can overwrite the recorded method of an already-settled GCASH payment). Each successful UPDATE then fires `createNotification(worker.worker_uid, { type:'earnings_payout', title:'Payment Received', ... })` at :97-105 and :133-141 with no `notificationKey`, so the ON CONFLICT dedupe at notification.service.ts:766-776 cannot engage. Both routes are live for the provider app: ServanaWorker/lib/core/api/servana_api.dart:394 (`POST /api/$bookingId/approve`) and :397 (`POST /api/$bookingId/mark-cash-paid`). Note the same absence of a state guard means a booking can be re-settled after a refund flips the status back.
findings.recommendation: Add `AND status <> 'PAID'` to both UPDATEs and treat zero rows as a successful no-op returning the existing payment row (replay-safe, not an error). Pass `notificationKey: 'bk<id>-paid'` to both createNotification calls so a duplicate never reaches the provider. Backend-only; ServanaWorker is unaffected because a replay keeps returning success.

findings.title: The booking OTP step still has no recovery: Resend calls a route that does not exist, and confirmOtp is still non-atomic so an assignment failure is reported as a bad code
findings.summary: First-pass SC-024 and SC-028, both re-verified unchanged. Together they make PENDING_OTP a one-way street: if the emailed code goes astray the only escape is broken, and if anything downstream of the status transition throws, the customer is told their correct code is wrong — permanently, because the UPDATE is guarded on a status that no longer matches.
findings.evidence: Resend: `grep -rn "resend-otp" src/` across servana_api-main returns zero hits; src/routes/booking.routes.ts registers no such path. The client calls it unconditionally at servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:409-413, from booking_otp_screen.dart:131-132, and reports 'Could not resend code. Please try again.' at :138-140. Atomicity: servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:140-150 commits `SET status='CONFIRMED' ... AND status='PENDING_OTP'` first; :185 then throws `Address missing locationId.`, :187 calls getLatLonByLocationId (which throws the bare string 'Location not found' — so `e.message` is undefined at bookingController.ts:77 and the body carries no message), and :190 calls assignNearestWorker — all inside the same try, all rethrown at :198-200, all mapped to HTTP 400 by bookingController.ts:76-78. On the second attempt the guarded UPDATE matches zero rows and returns 'Invalid OTP or booking is not in PENDING_OTP.' (:152-154). The OTP screen shows whichever message arrives, or 'Invalid code. Please try again.' (booking_otp_screen.dart:163-173). Compounding: the screen tells the customer the code came by SMS (booking_otp_screen.dart:249-250) while bookingService.ts:105-120 emails it.
findings.recommendation: Backend-only and unchanged from the first pass: add `POST /api/:id/resend-otp` with verifyAuth + assertBookingAccess, rate-limited and gated on PENDING_OTP (the client's path string already matches, so this closes with no release); wrap the status transition and tracking insert in a transaction and move assignNearestWorker out of the request-failure path; make confirmOtp idempotent so a repeated correct code on an already-CONFIRMED booking returns success; and normalise thrown strings to Error objects so §21 messages survive.

findings.title: Logout is still purely local — the client never calls POST /api/auth/logout, and the FCM clear that would work fires after the session is deleted
findings.summary: First-pass SC-038 and SC-086, both re-verified unchanged — no lib/ code shipped between the passes. The backend endpoint the client's TODO is waiting for has existed the whole time. A token captured before sign-out stays valid until natural expiry, and the device's FCM token is never cleared server-side because the teardown call is made after the bearer is gone.
findings.evidence: servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/http_backend.dart:163-167 — `Future<void> logout() async { }` with a TODO awaiting a backend endpoint. That endpoint exists: servana_api-main/src/routes/auth.route.ts:62 `router.post("/auth/logout", verifyAuth, authController.logoutController)`, and the controller runs `revokeTokenInFirebase(uid)` and `clearFcmToken(uid)`. Ordering: servana_client-main/lib/modules/authentication/presentation/bloc/authentication_bloc.dart calls `repo.logout()` (the no-op) then `await SessionService.deleteSession()` at :308, and only at :357 `await dpLocator<FcmCoordinator>().deactivateOnLogout()` → servana_api_client.dart:514-518 → `DELETE /api/user/fcm-token`, which is behind verifyAuth (servana_api-main/src/routes/user.route.ts:33) and now receives no Authorization header because `_headers()` (servana_api_client.dart:37-47) finds no session. The comment at authentication_bloc.dart:309-312 shows the resulting 401 was anticipated and suppressed rather than fixed. Confirmed no change: `git diff --stat bab66e4..4868aca` shows no authentication_bloc.dart or http_backend.dart edit.
findings.recommendation: Replace the no-op with a real `POST /api/auth/logout` call and move both it and `deactivateOnLogout()` above `SessionService.deleteSession()` (authentication_bloc.dart:308), wrapped in try/catch so a network failure still clears local state. Remove the stale TODO and the 401-normalising comment. Client-side; folds into the next scheduled release.

findings.title: Live provider tracking never plots the provider — the backend wraps the location doc under `location`, the client only unwraps `data` or the root
findings.hardRule: §4 additive compatibility, §9 no duplicate reality, §20 no ghost success
findings.summary: GET /api/workers/location/:uid returns `{success:true, location:{uid,isOnline,loc,updatedAt}}`. The customer app's parser looks for `loc` at the root, then falls back to `map['data']` — it never looks under `location`. So `raw['loc']` is always null and GeoPositionSnapshot.fromApiMap returns null on every successful 200. getProviderLocation is the ONLY source of the provider marker, so the live-tracking map silently renders with no provider position and no error — the customer is shown a tracking screen that structurally cannot work. Note this is the same envelope-vs-parser class as the options-with-addons 404 that 65b4337 fixed, one route over.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/controllers/technicianController.ts:177-180 — `return res.json({ success: true, location: toCamel(location) })`; the Mongo projection is `{uid, is_online, loc, updatedAt}` (services/technicianService.ts:376-390), so `loc` exists but one level down. servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/data/tracking_data_source.dart:33-38 — `final doc = result['data'] is Map ? result['data'] : result;` then `GeoPositionSnapshot.fromApiMap(doc)`. servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot.dart:46-51 — `final raw = map['loc'] != null ? map : (map['data'] ?? map); final loc = raw['loc']; if (loc == null) return null;`. With `doc = {success:true, location:{...}}` both branches miss and it returns null. Sole consumer chain: tracking_repository.dart:43,67,94 → booking_tracking_state.dart:34,69 → tracking_map.dart:86,109,143,170,177 (the provider marker is drawn only from state.providerLocation). No other producer of providerLocation exists in lib/.
findings.recommendation: Fix on the backend so no protected release is needed: at technicianController.ts:177-180 emit the doc's own keys alongside the envelope — `res.json({ success: true, location: doc, ...doc })` or, cleaner, add `data: doc` which the client's existing `result['data']` branch already handles. Purely additive; ServanaWorker and any other consumer keep reading `location`. Then, when the customer app is next opened, migrate it to the authenticated booking-scoped successor GET /api/booking/:bookingId/provider-location (provider.routes.ts:178), whose envelope is `{success, assigned, location}` — note that route has the identical unwrapping problem, so fix the shape once and use it for both.

findings.title: Cancelled bookings still occupy the provider's calendar — three availability queries match only the single-L 'CANCELED'
findings.hardRule: §13 canonical status, §29 provider eligibility, §9 no duplicate reality
findings.summary: Same status-vocabulary split as the payment-retry finding, with a different blast radius. Three conflict/busy queries exclude `'COMPLETED','CANCELED'` from bookings.status, but cancellation writes `'CANCELLED'`. A cancelled booking therefore permanently marks its provider busy for a ±2h window: auto-assignment filters them out, and admin assignment throws 'Worker is not available at ...'. Cancelling a booking silently destroys that slot's capacity forever. This compounds the still-open first-pass finding that assignNearestWorker returning {assigned:false} is silently discarded — the customer's next booking in that window is stranded at CONFIRMED with no provider and no error.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/services/technicianService.ts:570-579 (busy-UID set for assignment, `AND status NOT IN ('COMPLETED','CANCELED')`), :826-833 (available-worker filter, same predicate), :897-906 (explicit conflict check that throws 'Worker is not available at …' at :908-910). The only writers of the cancelled value are bookingService.ts:566 and adminBookingService.ts:937, both `'CANCELLED'`. Corroborating undercount on the same split: bookingService.ts:443 `COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'CANCELED') AS canceled`, surfaced as the 'CANCELED' dashboard bucket at :462 — it can only ever report 0. The correct both-spellings pattern already exists in the codebase at adminBookingService.ts:191, :252, :328, :713, :887, :932.
findings.recommendation: Backend-only, additive. Introduce one exported constant (e.g. `TERMINAL_BOOKING_STATUSES = ['COMPLETED','CANCELLED','CANCELED']`) and use it at technicianService.ts:577, :831, :901, bookingService.ts:443 and scheduler.ts:103. Do not change the stored value — 'CANCELLED' is what both mobile apps and the admin portal read (§4). Add a test: cancel a booking, then assert the same provider is returned as available for that time window.

findings.title: 880d5bc repaired the guest booking LIST but not the sibling ownership resolver — an admin-linked guest booking appears in the customer's list and 403s on tap
findings.hardRule: §10 one canonical capability, §9 no duplicate reality, §8 guest identity, §20 no ghost success
findings.summary: BOOKING.OWNERSHIP.RESOLVE is still implemented twice with different rules — the first pass recorded this and 880d5bc changed only one of the two. The list query now widens to guest bookings via the audited `gc.linked_customer_uid` link (correct, §8). resolveBookingAccess, which gates detail, tracking, gcash-submit and paymongo/create, knows nothing about that link: it grants 'customer' only when `bookings.user_id === actorUid`, and guest bookings have NULL user_id. So the exact bookings the admin deliberately linked to a client render in that client's Bookings tab and then return 403 BOOKING_ACCESS_DENIED on open. The defect survived the fix in a new form rather than being closed.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:366-372 — `WHERE (b.user_id = $1 OR b.guest_customer_id IN (SELECT gc.guest_customer_id FROM guest_customers gc WHERE gc.linked_customer_uid = $1))`. servana_api-main/src/services/bookingAccessService.ts:66-75 — `SELECT user_id FROM bookings WHERE id = $1` … `if (ownerUid && ownerUid === actorUid) return 'customer'`; no guest_customers join anywhere in the file, and the docblock at :53-57 still asserts guest bookings are provider/admin-only, which the list query no longer honours. Consumers that break: bookingController.ts:92 (getBooking), :153 (getTracking), paymentController.ts:14 (gcashSubmit), :80 (createPaymongoPayment) — all call assertBookingAccess, which throws 403 (bookingAccessService.ts:101-113). Client path: servana_api_client.dart:328-334 (list) then :387-391 / :463-465 (detail by tapping a row).
findings.recommendation: Backend-only, additive: teach resolveBookingAccess the same link the list already trusts — after the user_id comparison at bookingAccessService.ts:75, add `SELECT 1 FROM guest_customers gc JOIN bookings b ON b.guest_customer_id = gc.guest_customer_id WHERE b.id = $1 AND gc.linked_customer_uid = $2` and return 'customer' on a hit. That makes one capability out of two and removes the tap-then-403. Update the docblock at :53-57, which now states the opposite of the list's behaviour. Add a contract test asserting: every booking id returned by getBookingsByUserId(u) satisfies resolveBookingAccess(id, u) !== null.

findings.title: POST /api/:bookingId/paymongo/create is now authorized but still has no booking-state guard — a customer can mint a live checkout for their own cancelled or already-paid booking
findings.hardRule: §43 payment separation, §18 stale state, §17 idempotency, ALIGN §8
findings.summary: 52667b3 correctly answered 'whose booking is this' with assertBookingAccess. It did not answer 'is this booking still payable'. createCheckoutSession selects only id and final_price, so the route happily returns a live PayMongo checkout_url for a booking the customer already cancelled, or already paid. Every call also creates a brand-new session for the same booking with no idempotency, so a double-tap or a retry after the client's 30s timeout produces two payable links for one intent. Paying either lands on the webhook, which writes bookings.status='PAID' with no state predicate.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/controllers/paymentController.ts:77-98 — assertBookingAccess at :80, then straight to `paymentService.createCheckoutSession(bookingId)` at :82 with no status read. servana_api-main/src/services/paymentService.ts:155-170 — `SELECT b.id, b.final_price FROM bookings b WHERE b.id = $1`; b.status is never selected or checked, and there is no lookup of an existing open session. Client: servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:450-456 (createPaymongoSession sends no idempotency key at all, unlike createBooking at :369-385 which does send X-Idempotency-Key), behind a 30s timeout (:14, :883-897). Downstream: paymentService.ts webhook writes bookings.status='PAID' unconditionally (first-pass SC-053, verified still open).
findings.recommendation: Backend-only, no protected release. In createCheckoutSession select b.status and throw a safe domain error (e.g. BOOKING_NOT_PAYABLE, 409) for CANCELLED/CANCELED/COMPLETED, and for a payments row already at PAID. Reuse any existing non-expired provider_payment_id for the same booking instead of creating a second session, which gives the route idempotency without a client change. The same guard also fixes the scheduler path in the P0 above — one function, two callers.

findings.title: POST /api/:bookingId/resend-otp still does not exist — the OTP screen's only recovery path always fails
findings.hardRule: §4 additive compatibility, §20 no ghost success, ALIGN §0.4
findings.summary: Re-verified on the current backend: a grep of the whole of src/ for resend-otp / resendOtp returns nothing, and no router registers a POST matching /api/:id/resend-otp (booking.routes.ts registers only confirm-otp, :id and :id/tracking under that shape). The client's 'Resend code' button is live and reachable. The customer's only recourse when the OTP email does not arrive is a button that always errors, leaving the booking stranded in PENDING_OTP. Reported in the first pass (STITCH) and untouched by any of the nine commits; recording it here because it is a live customer-contract mismatch inside the ALIGN remit and the flow it blocks (booking confirmation) is primary.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main: `grep -rn 'resend-otp\|resendOtp\|resendBookingOtp' src/` returns zero matches; src/routes/booking.routes.ts:36-38 are the only /:id-shaped routes and none is resend-otp; src/routes/auth.route.ts:52 has resend-email-otp, a different capability. servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:409-413 — `POST /api/$bookingId/resend-otp`, with the client's own ALIGN-C07-001 warning at :406-408. servana_client-main/lib/common/presentation/screens/booking_otp_screen.dart:130-143 (calls it, catch-all sets 'Could not resend code'), :305 (the button). Note the error path is at least honest — no ghost success — but there is no working path at all.
findings.recommendation: Backend-only, additive: register `router.post('/:id/resend-otp', verifyAuth, bookingController.resendOtp)` in booking.routes.ts (before the /:id wildcard), have the controller call assertBookingAccess then re-send the existing bookings.otp_code via the same mailer the create path uses, rate-limited and idempotent on (bookingId, 60s). No protected release — the client already calls exactly this path. Separately correct the screen copy, which tells the customer the code was sent by SMS while the backend emails it (first-pass STITCH P2).

findings.title: Residual fail-open ownership shape and stale comments survive bd8c355 in listUserBookings
findings.summary: The route is now hard verifyAuth so this is unreachable today, but the controller still guards with the `actor?.uid &&` shape the removed middleware was paired with, and its comment asserts the opposite of current behaviour ('Mobile clients call without a token — unauthenticated path is unchanged for parity'). A future reader restoring an optional-auth variant, or mounting this handler on another router, reintroduces the anonymous bypass. The same shape in customerCancelBooking is not merely latent — see the P0 above.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/controllers/bookingController.ts:133-137 — `// When the caller has a verified JWT (browser session), enforce ownership. // Mobile clients call without a token — unauthenticated path is unchanged for parity.` followed by `const actor = (req as any).user; if (actor?.uid && actor.uid !== userId) return 403`. The route in front is hard auth (booking.routes.ts:21). Identical shape at src/controllers/user.controller.ts:168. The orphaned middleware src/middleware/verifyAuthOptional.ts still exists unimported and, unlike verifyAuth.ts:54-59, carries no NODE_ENV guard on its tempId bypass.
findings.recommendation: Backend-only cleanup, zero behaviour change: rewrite both guards as `if (!actor?.uid || actor.uid !== userId) return 403` so the check is fail-closed on its own terms, delete the stale comments, and delete src/middleware/verifyAuthOptional.ts now that nothing imports it (bd8c355 already removed every usage).

findings.title: Verified still open and unchanged: 17 of the 19 unfixed first-pass ALIGN findings
findings.summary: Re-checked against the current backend so the parent agent does not have to. All still stand exactly as first reported; none was accidentally fixed or worsened by the nine commits. Listing with fresh line numbers rather than re-filing them as findings.
findings.evidence: SC-045 X-Idempotency-Key unread: bookingController.ts:9-53 reads no header. SC-048 no service identity: bookingService.ts:320-378 joins payments/branches/user_address/booking_workers only — no service_options join, no serviceName. SC-049 no canonical status: formatBooking emits only status + `statusLower: statusVal.toLowerCase()` (bookingService.ts:519); mapOperationsStatus remains admin-only (adminBookingService.ts:191). SC-050 one customer-notification producer: `grep -rn 'createCustomerNotification('` outside notification.service.ts returns exactly one hit, bookingController.ts:38. SC-052 zero customer audit events: auditFire appears in 10 files, all admin controllers/services + requirePermission.ts — no customer path. SC-053 webhook overwrites bookings.status='PAID' unguarded. SC-054 two timelines: cancel INSERTs into booking_timeline_events (bookingService.ts:576-585) while getTracking SELECTs booking_tracking (:379-390). SC-096 tracking rows run through the booking formatter: bookingController.ts:161 `formatBookings(tracking)` and the unconditional `bookingCode:` at bookingService.ts:508 → 'SVN-undefined' on every event. SC-051 email-OTP identity, SC-046 guestCustomerId in customerUid, SC-047/SC-098/SC-117 client-side items, SC-094 settle idempotency, SC-095 tracking vocabulary, SC-097 logout, SC-099 premature conversation, SC-101 route shapes, SC-102 payment envelopes — all unchanged. Only SC-003, SC-004 (partially), SC-044 and SC-100 were addressed.
findings.recommendation: No new action beyond the first pass's recommendations. Priority order given the new findings: land the shared cancelled-status constant (fixes my P0-2 and P1-2 together), then the state guard in createCheckoutSession (fixes my P1-5 and hardens P0-2), then assertBookingAccess in customerCancelBooking (my P0-1), then SC-053's conditional webhook UPDATE, which is the last step in the pay-a-cancelled-booking chain.
findings.fixLocation: see docs/audit/ALIGN_CLIENT.md in servana_client-main for the per-finding targets

findings.title: FCM token deactivation on logout always 401s — the session is deleted before the call that needs it
findings.summary: AuthLogout deletes the Hive session at step 3 and calls FcmCoordinator.deactivateOnLogout() at step 7. That coordinator's DELETE /api/user/fcm-token goes through ServanaApiClient, which builds its headers by reading the session that no longer exists — so the request ships with no Authorization header, verifyAuth rejects it, and the server keeps user A's device token bound to user A. The exception is swallowed, so the app reports a clean logout. Rated P2 rather than P0 only because FirebaseMessaging.instance.deleteToken() on the next line kills the token registration on Firebase's side; that call is itself best-effort and swallowed, so on a device that is offline at logout the stale server-side binding is the only thing left.
findings.evidence: servana_client-main/lib/modules/authentication/presentation/bloc/authentication_bloc.dart:308 `await SessionService.deleteSession();` — then :359 `await dpLocator<FcmCoordinator>().deactivateOnLogout();`. servana_client-main/lib/modules/notifications/application/fcm_coordinator.dart:85-87 `try { await _repository.clearFcmToken(); } catch (_) {}` → notifications_repository.dart:53 → notifications_remote_data_source.dart:37-39 → servana_api_client.dart:514. servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:37-46 `_headers()` — `final session = await SessionService.getSession(); final token = session?.token; if (token != null && token.isNotEmpty) { ...Bearer... } return {'Content-Type': 'application/json'};` — no session means no header. servana_api-main/src/routes/user.route.ts:33 `router.delete("/user/fcm-token", verifyAuth, userController.clearCustomerFcmToken)` and src/middleware/verifyAuth.ts:13-20 return 401 when neither an Authorization header nor a __session cookie is present. The mitigation is servana_client-main/lib/modules/notifications/application/fcm_coordinator.dart:90-92 `try { await FirebaseMessaging.instance.deleteToken(); } catch (_) {}`.
findings.recommendation: Move the FCM deactivation above the session delete in authentication_bloc.dart — capture the token, call deactivateOnLogout(), then SessionService.deleteSession(). The 'set guest status before cleanup so a 401 does not show Session expired' comment at :309-313 is why the order is what it is; keep that property by suppressing onUnauthorized for the logout window rather than by deleting the session first. ServanaClient is protected (§1), so this needs authorization and a release — or, if a release is unacceptable, make the backend accept the deletion when the caller presents a still-valid Firebase ID token via the existing verifyAuth path before local teardown.

findings.title: Admin-linked guest bookings are listed to the linked customer but cannot be opened — assertBookingAccess ignores the link
findings.hardRule: §8 guest customer / §9 no duplicate reality / §20 no ghost success
findings.summary: 880d5bc correctly made the list query surface guest bookings through gc.linked_customer_uid. But the booking-detail authorization primitive only ever compares bookings.user_id, which is NULL on those rows. So the customer sees the booking in their list and gets a 403 the moment they tap it. Not a leak — the failure is closed — but it is a half-wired feature that will read as a bug in production, and any future 'fix' applied at the wrong layer is how the NULL-owner class of hole gets reintroduced.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:365-372 — `WHERE (b.user_id = $1 OR b.guest_customer_id IN (SELECT gc.guest_customer_id FROM guest_customers gc WHERE gc.linked_customer_uid = $1))`. servana_api-main/src/services/bookingAccessService.ts:66-75 — resolves `SELECT user_id FROM bookings WHERE id = $1` and returns 'customer' only via `if (ownerUid && ownerUid === actorUid)`; there is no guest_customers lookup anywhere in the file. The doc comment at :52-57 states the intent ('such bookings stay visible to the assigned provider and to admins only'), which directly contradicts what the list query now returns. Consumers affected: servana_api-main/src/routes/booking.routes.ts:37 (GET /:id) and :38 (tracking), both of which ServanaClient calls.
findings.recommendation: Extend resolveBookingAccess to accept the same explicit link: after the user_id comparison, check `SELECT 1 FROM guest_customers WHERE guest_customer_id = <booking.guest_customer_id> AND linked_customer_uid = $actorUid`. Return 'customer' on a hit. Keep it to that one audited column — never fall back to phone matching, which is the bug 880d5bc removed. Then update the stale comment at bookingAccessService.ts:52-57.

findings.title: A provider removed from a booking keeps the conversation in their chat inbox
findings.hardRule: §11 removed provider → future messages / §22 reassignment revokes access
findings.summary: Message bodies are properly protected — every read path re-derives access from booking_workers with an active-status filter, so a declined or reassigned provider gets 403 on the conversation and its messages. But the inbox listing is driven off chat_participants, and participant rows are only ever upserted, never removed when an assignment ends. The removed provider therefore keeps seeing the conversation row and its unread counter. Metadata only: chat_conversations carries booking_id, is_closed and last_message_at, not message text.
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/src/chat/chat.repository.ts:258-274 listConversationsForUser — `FROM chat_conversations c JOIN chat_participants p ON p.conversation_id = c.id WHERE p.user_uid = $1`, with an unread_count subquery, and no join back to booking_workers. servana_api-main/src/chat/chat.service.ts:59-78 getOrCreateConversation only calls repo.upsertParticipant for the client and for the CURRENTLY active workers (:71-75) — nothing ever deletes a row for a worker who has left. By contrast the read paths are correct: chat.service.ts:35-38 resolveAccessForBooking checks repo.getBookingWorkerUids, which filters `status IN ('ASSIGNED','ACCEPTED','IN_PROGRESS','COMPLETED')` (chat.repository.ts:72-81), and getMessages (:215-217), sendMessage (:131-133), getConversation (chat.controller.ts:60-61) and the socket join (chat.gateway.ts:75-76) all gate on it.
findings.recommendation: Either delete the participant row when an assignment is revoked (in the reassign/decline paths), or — safer and additive — have listConversationsForUser re-derive membership the same way the read paths do, e.g. by intersecting the participant join with resolveAccessForBooking's predicate rather than trusting the participant table alone. The service must remain the single source of membership truth (§9).

findings.title: Stale comments claim no customer cancel endpoint exists, while the client already calls one
findings.hardRule: §62 completion reports must reflect actual results
findings.summary: Two ServanaClient comments assert that cancellation hits an admin-only route and will 403 for customer tokens. The client actually posts to the customer route, which exists and is authenticated. Harmless today, but it is exactly the kind of drift that leads a future reader to 'fix' authorization in the wrong direction.
findings.evidence: servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/data/booking_repository.dart:69-74 — 'BACKEND_GAP-C15-001: No customer-facing cancel endpoint exists. This method calls the admin endpoint and will receive HTTP 403 for non-admin tokens... Once a POST /api/<id>/cancel customer route exists...'. Same claim at servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/presentation/widgets/booking_cancellation_sheet.dart:82. What it actually calls: servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:476 `final uri = _uri('/api/bookings/$bookingId/cancel');` — which is served by servana_api-main/src/routes/booking.routes.ts:30 with verifyAuth.
findings.recommendation: Delete the two BACKEND_GAP-C15-001 comments. Documentation-only; batch it into whatever the next authorized ServanaClient release is rather than cutting one for it.

findings.title: PROVIDER.LOCATION.READ has three response shapes and ServanaClient parses none — live tracking never shows the provider
findings.hardRule: §9 no duplicate reality · §4 additive compatibility · §20 no ghost success · REPEAT Class A/C
findings.summary: One capability, two backend routes, three envelope shapes, and the customer app's parser matches none of them. GeoPositionSnapshot.fromApiMap returns null on every real response, so the live-tracking map silently never renders the provider marker. The unit tests are green because their fixtures were written against a shape the backend does not emit — the same failure mode the options-with-addons fix was written to call out, recurring one module over.
findings.evidence:
Legacy route: servana_api-main/src/controllers/technicianController.ts:177-180 returns `{ success: true, location: toCamel(location) }`. Successor route (added in a85998e): src/controllers/providerLocationAccessController.ts:85 returns `{ success: true, assigned: true, location }` with the raw Mongo doc, un-camelised — so `is_online` vs `isOnline` also diverge between the two members of one capability family. Underlying canonical read is shared (technicianService.ts:376-391 projects `{uid, is_online, loc, updatedAt}`), so this is presentation drift, not two sources of truth.

Client: servana_client-main/lib/modules/tracking/data/tracking_data_source.dart:34-37 computes `doc = result['data'] is Map ? result['data'] : result`. The legacy response has no `data` key, so `doc` becomes the whole envelope `{success, location:{...}}`. lib/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot.dart:47-51 then evaluates `map['loc']` (null — it is nested under `location`), falls back to `map['data']` (absent), sets `raw = map`, reads `raw['loc']` (null) and returns null. Every successful 200 yields null.

The failure is swallowed twice over: tracking_data_source.dart:39-41 converts 404 to null, and tracking_repository.dart:43-47 and :67-70 wrap the call in `.catchError((e) => null)`, so `providerLocation: null` (tracking_repository.dart:94) is indistinguishable from 'provider has not reported a position'. tracking_map.dart:177 draws the provider marker only `if (widget.state.providerLocation != null)` — so the marker is unconditionally absent.

Tests certify the wrong shape: test/modules/tracking/domain/geo_position_snapshot_test.dart:8-14 builds fixtures with `loc` at the root, and :24-28 tests a `data` envelope. Neither is what any backend route returns. test/modules/tracking/data/tracking_repository_test.dart mocks the data source, so it never touches the envelope either.

Migration state, since this is the REPEAT question: ServanaClient is still on the legacy route (servana_api_client.dart:350-354), and so is ServanaWorker (ServanaWorker/lib/core/api/servana_api.dart:316, :319, :322). Step 2 of docs/WORKER_ROUTE_MIGRATION.md has not begun for either mobile app; the /worker/* family currently has no mobile consumer at all.
findings.recommendation: Two moves, in this order. (1) Backend, additive, no client release: have the legacy handler also emit the document under the key the client already probes — `res.json({ success: true, location: toCamel(doc), data: toCamel(doc) })` at technicianController.ts:177. tracking_data_source.dart:34 checks `result['data']` first, so this alone restores the marker on the installed base. (2) Converge the two shapes: make the successor return `location: toCamel(doc)` so the family has one projection, then point the client at `GET /booking/:bookingId/provider-location` in the next release. That migration is now nearly free — the client's parser needs a fix either way, and fixing it once against `result['location'] ?? result['data'] ?? result` satisfies both routes. Add a fixture to geo_position_snapshot_test.dart copied verbatim from a real response body of each route, not hand-written.

findings.title: BOOKING.DETAIL.READ has no audience projection — the sibling 65b4337 missed; the assigned provider receives the customer's OTP and GCash payment evidence
findings.hardRule: §58 privacy · §43 payment evidence · §9 no duplicate reality · REPEAT Class C
findings.summary: 65b4337 fixed PROVIDER.PROFILE.READ by adding projectProviderProfile — one canonical service, three authorised projections. The identical Class C defect on BOOKING.DETAIL.READ was left in place: GET /api/:id selects `b.*` and the formatter spreads every column, so all three audiences (customer, actively-assigned provider, admin) receive one identical, maximal object. That object carries `otpCode` and the customer's GCash reference number and payment-proof URL.
findings.evidence:
servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:207-238 (`getBookingById`) selects `b.*` plus `p.status, p.method, p.reference_no, p.proof_url`. `bookings.otp_code` is a real column — written at bookingService.ts:78 and :89 on creation, matched at :145 on confirm. formatBooking (bookingService.ts:494-522) begins `const c = toCamel(raw)` and returns `{ ...c, ...aliases }`, spreading every selected column; the doc comment at :480 states the intent outright — 'Keeps every field toCamel() produces'. bookingController.ts:100 returns `{ success: true, booking: formatBooking(booking) }`.

Who reaches it: booking.routes.ts:37 is verifyAuth, and bookingController.ts:92 calls assertBookingAccess, which grants 'provider' to any uid holding a booking_workers row in ASSIGNED / ACCEPTED / IN_PROGRESS / COMPLETED (bookingAccessService.ts:36-41, :77-83). So the provider assigned to the job reads `otpCode`, `referenceNo` and `proofUrl` for that booking.

Scope of the OTP exposure, stated precisely rather than maximally: assignment happens inside confirmOtp (bookingService.ts:190 calls assignNearestWorker after the PENDING_OTP → CONFIRMED update at :137-149), so no provider can be attached while the OTP is still spendable. What leaks is a spent secret — a §58 violation ('do not expose OTP values'), not a reachable confirm-on-behalf escalation. The payment evidence is not spent: proof_url and reference_no are live at the moment the provider can read them.

Same shape on the list surface: bookingService.ts:284 and :329 also select `p.proof_url` for getBookingsByUserId and getTracking, against §58's 'list endpoints return only fields required by the list'.

No protected release: ServanaClient reads `json['workerCode']` and never `otpCode` — the customer app has explicitly given up the legacy alias (aircon_booking_store.dart:126-128: 'The legacy `otpCode` field is being deprecated by the BE; do not fall back to it'), and its own analytics redaction list names 'otp_code' as sensitive (lib/core/analytics/data/analytics_privacy_filter.dart:44). Grep for proofUrl / referenceNo across lib/ finds only a comment at http_backend.dart:346-348 stating the app 'never reads referenceNo'. Withholding all three from non-customer audiences breaks nothing.
findings.recommendation: Add projectBooking(booking, audience) beside providerProfileProjection.ts and reuse the audience resolver that already exists — assertBookingAccess (bookingAccessService.ts:101) already returns the role, so bookingController.ts:92 can pass it straight through instead of discarding it. Follow the same explicit-list discipline as providerProfileProjection.ts:52-56: withhold by default so a new column added to `b.*` is not silently published. Minimum withheld set for audience 'provider': otpCode, proofUrl, referenceNo. Drop proof_url from the getBookingsByUserId and getTracking SELECTs entirely (bookingService.ts:284, :329) — no caller reads it.

findings.title: legacyRouteTelemetry records no uid on 30 of the 36 legacy routes, and its test injects the field Express cannot supply
findings.hardRule: §60 run the checks · §34 observability · REPEAT §35 deprecation
findings.summary: The telemetry added in 65b4337 exists to produce the traffic numbers that gate step 4 of the worker-route migration and to detect uid enumeration. Because it is mounted as router.use() middleware, req.params is empty when it runs, so it can only see a uid on the four routes that pass ?workerUid= in the query string. The two routes the migration doc names as highest-risk — GET /workers/location/:uid and GET /workers/:workerId/job-cards — carry their uid in the path and are therefore logged as claimsUid=no and never counted toward the enumeration threshold.
findings.evidence:
servana_api-main/src/routes/technician.routes.ts:15 mounts `router.use("/workers", legacyRouteTelemetry)`. src/middleware/legacyRouteTelemetry.ts:72-76 resolves the claimed uid as `req.query?.workerUid || req.params?.uid || req.params?.workerId || ""`.

Proven by execution, not by reasoning about Express: a minimal app with `r.use('/workers', mw)` plus `r.get('/workers/location/:uid', ...)` mounted at `/api`, hit with GET /api/workers/location/UID-ABC, printed `IN USE MW: params= {} query= {}` from the middleware while the route handler received `{"uid":"UID-ABC"}`. A `.use()` layer's req.params carries only the mount path's own params, and `/workers` has none.

Consequence by route: of the 36 legacy routes, only the four lifecycle routes read a query uid (technicianController.ts:497, :526, :555, :583 read `req.query.workerUid`). The other 30 — including getLocation (technicianController.ts:159, `req.params.uid`), getJobCards (:216, `req.params.workerId`) and workerSchedule (:191) — take it from the path. So the `SUSPICIOUS_DISTINCT_UIDS` alarm (legacyRouteTelemetry.ts:35, :86-94) cannot fire for the enumeration that actually matters: pulling many providers' live positions, or many providers' job cards, each of which carries a customer's name, phone and street address.

The suite does not catch it because it bypasses Express entirely: tests/legacy-route-telemetry.test.ts:29 seeds `params: {}` on the fake request, then :113-115 call with `{params:{uid:'uid-a'}}` and `{params:{workerId:'uid-b'}}` and assert `__distinctUidsFor(SOURCE)` is 2. It asserts the middleware's arithmetic, never the wiring that feeds it.
findings.recommendation: Parse the uid from the URL rather than from req.params, which is the only source available at .use() time — e.g. match `req.path` against /^\/(?:location\/)?([^/]+)/ after the /workers mount, or move the middleware to a router.param('uid') plus router.param('workerId') registration, which does run with params bound. Then close the self-test gap the way the LAGDA probe rule prescribes: mount the real middleware on a real Express router in the test and drive it with supertest against `/api/workers/location/:uid`, so a positive fixture exists for a path-parameterised route and a regression cannot pass. Until this is fixed, treat any 'legacy traffic is low' reading as unmeasured, and do not let it satisfy step 4 of docs/WORKER_ROUTE_MIGRATION.md.

findings.title: JOB_CARD.READ has two independent formatters over one canonical query, and they disagree on address.instructions
findings.hardRule: §10 no duplicated domain logic · §9 no duplicate reality · §58 privacy
findings.summary: The legacy and successor job-card endpoints share the canonical read (technicianService.getJobCardsByWorker) but each hand-rolls its own response object. The shapes have drifted: the unauthenticated legacy route publishes the customer's delivery instructions and the authenticated successor does not. The migration doc lists this pair under 'Already available — the app can move today', which is true only because nothing consumes the extra field.
findings.evidence:
Both endpoints call the same service: servana_api-main/src/controllers/technicianController.ts:218 and src/controllers/providerController.ts:2015 / :2032 each call `technician.getJobCardsByWorker(...)`. The formatting is duplicated rather than shared — technicianController.ts:224-247 builds the object inline, providerController.ts:1995-2009 defines a separate `formatJobCard`, ironically commented 'Shared formatter to avoid duplication' while being the second of two.

The drift: technicianController.ts:242 emits `instructions: job.delivery_instructions ?? null` inside the address block. providerController.ts:2000 emits the same address block with addressOne, addressTwo, city, zipCode, country and label — and no instructions. Every other field matches, which is what makes the omission look accidental rather than deliberate.

Direction of the risk is the reverse of what the migration table implies. Delivery instructions are access information — gate codes, 'leave at the guard house', which unit. GET /api/workers/:workerId/job-cards has no auth (technician.routes.ts:39, and the file's own banner at :17 says so), so today an unauthenticated caller naming any worker uid receives them, while the token-scoped successor withholds them.

No live consumer either way: grep for 'instructions' across ServanaWorker/lib returns nothing, and ServanaWorker is still entirely on the legacy family (ServanaWorker/lib/core/api/servana_api.dart:322, features/homepage/data/job_cards_store.dart:12).
findings.recommendation: Collapse the two formatters into one exported function used by both controllers — the canonical read is already shared, so only the projection needs consolidating (§10). Resolve the field deliberately in one place rather than by omission: since no client reads delivery_instructions, drop it from the legacy shape too. That is the cheapest item on the migration doc's own 'Interim hardening' list, it removes customer access information from an unauthenticated endpoint, and it needs no protected release because the field has no consumer.

findings.title: createBooking returns the plaintext booking OTP to the caller as otpDevOnly, with no environment guard
findings.summary: The booking-creation response includes the OTP that was just emailed to the customer, under a field name asserting it is development-only. Nothing gates it on NODE_ENV. It defeats the point of mailing the code — possession of the mailbox is no longer required to confirm the booking — and it puts an OTP into every client log, crash report and proxy that captures the response body.
findings.evidence:
servana_api-main/src/services/bookingService.ts:121-128 returns `{ bookingId, status, quotedPrice, finalPrice, otpDevOnly: otp }`, where `otp` is the value generated at :71 and written to bookings.otp_code at :78/:89. There is no `process.env.NODE_ENV` check anywhere in the function. bookingController.ts:49 passes it straight out: `res.json({ success: true, booking })`. Contrast verifyAuth.ts:54-59, where the comparable dev bypass is explicitly environment-guarded — the pattern exists in this codebase and was not applied here.

The same value reaches the client a second way once REP-02 is understood: confirmOtp returns `formatBooking(booking)` (bookingController.ts:75), and formatBooking spreads `b.*`, so `otpCode` is in that response too.

No protected release: grep for `otpDevOnly` across servana_client-main/lib and test returns nothing — the customer app never reads it. It reads `json['workerCode']` (customer_booking.dart:229) and has explicitly abandoned the otpCode alias (aircon_booking_store.dart:126-128). The client's own analytics redaction filter lists 'otp_code' as a field to strip (lib/core/analytics/data/analytics_privacy_filter.dart:44), so the app already treats this as a secret the backend should not be sending.
findings.recommendation: Delete `otpDevOnly` from the bookingService.ts:127 return. If a development affordance is genuinely wanted, gate it the way verifyAuth.ts:54-59 gates its bypass — `...(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? { otpDevOnly: otp } : {})` — so production cannot emit it regardless of caller.

findings.title: Class F confirmed still live at 799b6aa: otp_code and worker_code are one generator behind two business meanings, and the assignment service returns worker_code under the key otpCode
findings.summary: Carried forward from the first pass (masterlist SC-107). Re-verified rather than re-reported, because the two secrets now travel in the same response object and the collision is one careless fallback away from showing a customer the wrong code. The client has already absorbed the cost in a hand-written warning comment.
findings.evidence:
servana_api-main/src/services/technicianService.ts:617 generates `const otpCode = generateOTP()`, writes it to a different column at :626 (`worker_code = $4`), and returns it to the caller under the original name at :694 (`otpCode`). Meanwhile bookingService.ts:71 generates a separate `otp` for `bookings.otp_code` — the email confirmation code — consumed at :145. One generator, two columns, two business meanings, one wire name.

Both columns now surface together on the same object: getBookingById selects `b.*` (bookingService.ts:210) and formatBooking spreads it (bookingService.ts:495, :504), so GET /api/:id emits `otpCode` (the email code) and `workerCode` (the start-job code) side by side.

The client bears the disambiguation: servana_client-main/lib/modules/aircon_booking/data/aircon_booking_store.dart:126-128 reads 'Canonical wire field is `workerCode`. The legacy `otpCode` field is being deprecated by the BE; do not fall back to it', duplicated at bw_booking_store.dart:116. The QR widget carries a versioned payload emitting both keys during the transition (qr_worker_code_display.dart:40-43). Verified the app is currently correct — customer_booking.dart:229 reads `json['workerCode']` with no otpCode fallback — so there is no live break, only a standing trap.
findings.recommendation: Rename the return key at technicianService.ts:694 from `otpCode` to `workerCode` so the wire name matches the column and the meaning. Register both names in the field alias registry (src/utils/fieldParity.ts already hosts this kind of entry) with an explicit conflict policy stating they are distinct entities and must never be merged, per §0.12. Then remove `otpCode` from the customer booking projection entirely as part of REP-02, which retires the collision rather than documenting it.

findings.title: CI never runs the test suite — all 1280 tests, including the nine new security regression suites, are unenforced on deploy
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/.github/workflows/deploy.yml is the only workflow (`ls .github/workflows/` → deploy.yml). Its full step list, from `grep -n 'name:\|run:'`: Fix workspace permissions (:14) → Checkout (:18) → Copy secrets (:21) → Require DB_PASSWORD (:34) → Run pending DB migrations (:44) → Use Node.js 24 (:152) → Install dependencies (:158, `npm ci`) → Build (:161-162, `npm run build`) → Restart PM2 (:164) → Reload NGINX (:172). There is no `npm test`, no `npm run test:ci`, no `npm run verify`, and no `npm run guard:protected-contracts` step anywhere in the file. package.json:11-13 defines all three scripts; nothing invokes them. `npm run build` is `tsc && cp ...` (package.json:8), so typecheck IS enforced — tests are not. This is the enabling condition for every other finding here: a revert of 52667b3, 6d78313, bd8c355 or 65b4337 deploys to production with a green pipeline. Note also that migrations run at :44, BEFORE the build at :162, so a compile failure leaves schema changes already applied.
findings.recommendation: Add a `- name: Test` step running `npm run verify` (typecheck + test:ci) and a `- name: Guard protected contracts` step running `npm run guard:protected-contracts`, both BEFORE `Run pending DB migrations` at deploy.yml:44 — not merely before Build, so a red suite cannot leave the database migrated. `node scripts/guard-protected-contracts.mjs` currently exits 0 in 1s, so neither step is costly.

findings.title: leak-isolation.test.js still green-asserts the vulnerability bd8c355 removed, and passes only because of a comment
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/tests/leak-isolation.test.js:123-127 reads `expect(src).toContain("verifyAuthOptional")` against src/routes/booking.routes.ts, under the describe title 'LEAK-FIX: listUserBookings enforces ownership when JWT present'. verifyAuthOptional was removed from that file by bd8c355 — the assertion passes today for one reason only: booking.routes.ts:14 begins `// Hard auth. This was verifyAuthOptional on a "mobile may call without a token"...`. Deleting or rewording that comment turns the test red, and the obvious remedy a developer applies to a red test named 'LEAK-FIX' is to re-add the middleware. tests/leak-isolation.test.js:134-146 compounds it, asserting `fs.existsSync(SRC('middleware','verifyAuthOptional.ts'))` is true and that the file contains no `status(401)` — pinning the orphaned middleware in existence and blocking its deletion. That file (src/middleware/verifyAuthOptional.ts:17-21) has a `tempId` dev bypass with NO NODE_ENV guard, unlike src/middleware/verifyAuth.ts:55-59 which calls `process.exit(1)` outside development/local/test. Separately, tests/leak-isolation.test.js:118-121 and tests/anonymous-bypass.test.ts:89-94 both assert the presence of `actor?.uid && actor.uid !== userId` (bookingController.ts:134-137) — so hardening that fail-open guard into `!actor || actor.uid !== userId` would break two tests, meaning the suite actively resists the correct fix.
findings.recommendation: Delete tests/leak-isolation.test.js:117-146 (both stale describes) and delete src/middleware/verifyAuthOptional.ts. Replace the two `actor?.uid &&` assertions at leak-isolation.test.js:120 and anonymous-bypass.test.ts:93 with an assertion of the fail-closed shape, and change the controllers to match. Add to tests/anonymous-bypass.test.ts a test that verifyAuthOptional.ts does not exist on disk, replacing the one that asserts it does.
