findings.title: verifyAuth.ts — the single middleware all nine security fixes rest on — has zero behavioural tests, including its production TEMP_ID kill-switch
findings.evidence: `grep -rln 'verifyAuth\b' tests/` returns 13 files, but every hit is a source-string assertion about a ROUTE file (e.g. tests/admin-guest.test.js:145 `expect(routes).toContain("import verifyAuth from '../middleware/verifyAuth'")`). No test imports src/middleware/verifyAuth.ts or invokes it. Untested behaviours that are all load-bearing right now: the 401 on a missing Authorization header AND missing `__session` cookie (verifyAuth.ts:13-20); the `__session` cookie path (:11, :23-24) which is a second, less obvious way to authenticate; the TOKEN_EXPIRED vs INVALID_TOKEN branch (:40-52); and critically the production kill-switch at :54-59, where a set `tempId` outside NODE_ENV in {development, local, test} calls `process.exit(1)`. `grep -rn 'tempId\|TEMP_ID\|NODE_ENV' tests/` returns nothing. If that guard is ever inverted or the DEV_ENVS set widened, every route hardened this session silently authenticates as a single fixed uid and 1280 tests stay green.
findings.recommendation: New file tests/verify-auth.test.ts: mock firebase-admin/auth and ../src/config, then cover — (a) no header, no cookie → 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and next() NOT called; (b) `__session` cookie alone authenticates; (c) `Bearer ` with empty token → 401, not a pass-through; (d) verifyIdToken rejecting with auth/id-token-expired → 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED, any other error → 401 INVALID_TOKEN; (e) tempId set with NODE_ENV='production' → process.exit called (spy on process.exit) and req.user NOT populated; (f) tempId set with NODE_ENV='test' → req.user = {uid: tempId}.

findings.title: Five of seven assertBookingAccess call sites have no controller test, and there is no catch-all that would have caught the original approve/mark-cash-paid miss
findings.evidence: `grep -rn assertBookingAccess src/` gives seven controller call sites. Covered: paymentController.ts:42 (tests/payment-settlement-access.test.ts) and providerLocationAccessController.ts:69 (tests/provider-location-access.test.ts). NOT covered by any test: bookingController.ts:71 (confirmOtp), :92 (getBooking), :153 (getTracking), paymentController.ts:14 (gcashSubmit), :80 (createPaymongoPayment). tests/booking-access.test.ts tests the predicate resolveBookingAccess/assertBookingAccess in isolation — it proves the lock works, never that these five doors use it. This is precisely the failure mode the first pass found: approve and markCashPaid were missed when gcashSubmit was fixed, because nothing enumerated the family. The suite still has no such enumeration, so the next handler added to bookingController or paymentController can omit the guard with a green pipeline. Note the guard is doing real work at these sites: getTracking and getBooking return the customer's name, phone and home address, and booking ids are sequential integers (tests/booking-access.test.ts:5-7).
findings.recommendation: Extend tests/booking-access.test.ts (or a new tests/booking-scoped-handlers.test.ts) with two layers. (1) A describe.each over all five handlers, mocking bookingAccessService the way payment-settlement-access.test.ts:17-39 does, asserting each: refuses when the guard rejects, does not call its service when refused, and calls the guard BEFORE the service (the mockImplementation-ordering trick at payment-settlement-access.test.ts:135-138). (2) A source-level catch-all in the spirit of leak-isolation.test.js:75-85: parse src/routes/booking.routes.ts and src/routes/payment.routes.ts, and for every non-webhook handler they name, assert the exported function body in the corresponding controller contains `assertBookingAccess` — so a new booking-scoped route cannot ship unguarded.

findings.title: createBooking's identity-from-token fix — the core of 52667b3 for the customer app — has no test of any kind
findings.evidence: src/controllers/bookingController.ts:16 sets `const userId = (req as any).user?.uid`, :17-22 accepts and deliberately ignores a mismatched `?userId=`, and :23-29 401s when the token yields no uid. `grep -rn 'createBooking' tests/*.ts tests/*.js` returns only tests/admin-create-booking.test.js (which tests adminCreateBookingService, a different code path, and at :200 asserts it does NOT call createBooking) and a bare comment at tests/admin-booking.test.ts:307. Nothing asserts that a request carrying `?userId=<victim>` with attacker-A's token creates the booking under A, nor that the parameter remains accepted so ServanaClient keeps working — servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart still passes `userId` on createBooking, so the backward-compatibility half is a live protected-client contract with zero coverage. A revert to `req.query.userId` restores booking-creation-in-anyone's-name and the suite stays green.
findings.recommendation: Add to tests/booking-access.test.ts or a new tests/create-booking-identity.test.ts: mock bookingService and notification.service, then assert (a) `bookingService.createBooking` receives the token uid when `?userId=` is absent; (b) it receives the TOKEN uid, not the query uid, when they differ, and a warning is logged containing no uid (§58); (c) it receives the token uid unchanged when `?userId=` matches — the compatibility case ServanaClient exercises; (d) a request with `req.user` undefined returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and never calls the service.

findings.title: resolveProviderAudience is untested — the projection tests prove the filter works but never that it is applied to the right callers
findings.evidence: src/controllers/technicianController.ts:88-89 resolves the audience and :93 applies it; the decision function is at technicianController.ts:1022-1038. `grep -rn resolveProviderAudience tests/` returns nothing. tests/provider-profile-projection.test.ts covers projectProviderProfile exhaustively but passes the audience literal in by hand (:42 `'other'`, :91 `'self'`, :95 `'admin'`), so the whole projection is bypassed if the resolver is wrong and no test fires. The resolver's fail-closed properties are all currently correct and all unprotected: `if (!actorUid) return 'other'` (:1026), the self short-circuit (:1027), `Number(rows[0].role) === 1` (:1033), and — most importantly — `catch { return 'other' }` at :1034-1036, where a DB error must not widen access. Flipping that catch to return 'admin' restores the original P0 (email, birthdate, home addresses, compliance documents, booking history naming every customer served, disbursement ledger, earnings) to any authenticated caller, with 1280 tests green.
findings.recommendation: Add a describe block to tests/provider-profile-projection.test.ts mocking ../src/db/dbQuery and ../src/config: (a) undefined actorUid → 'other' with NO query issued; (b) actorUid === subjectUid → 'self' with no query issued; (c) role 1 → 'admin'; (d) role 2 and role 3 → 'other'; (e) zero rows → 'other'; (f) dbQuery.query rejecting → 'other', not 'admin'. Then one integration-shaped test over getByUid itself asserting that a role-2 caller's response body contains none of WITHHELD_FROM_OTHERS.

findings.title: Two test suites are silently excluded from jest, and they are the only ones that exercise real HTTP routes
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/jest.config.js:5 sets `testPathIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/', 'admin-dedup\\.test\\.ts$', 'catalog-service\\.test\\.ts$']`. tests/ holds 31 files; `npx jest --listTests | wc -l` returns 29. The exclusion is technically justified — both are standalone ts-node scripts with their own pass/fail counters that require a live server (`Run with: npx ts-node tests/catalog-service.test.ts (Requires local API on PORT env var or default 3000)`, catalog-service.test.ts:10-11; same at admin-dedup.test.ts:8-9) — but the consequence is that NOTHING enforces them, and nothing replaces them. `grep -rlE 'supertest|from .\.\./src/app' tests/` returns no match and package.json lists no supertest dependency: all 1280 running tests are unit or source-regex assertions, and not one request ever traverses the express middleware chain. Concretely, the `/services/:serviceId/options-with-addons` alias added by 65b4337 (src/routes/service.route.ts:24) — which servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:264 calls — is asserted only at catalog-service.test.ts:137-163, i.e. never.
findings.recommendation: Add supertest, and create tests/route-contract.test.ts mounting the express app with firebase-admin and the pg pool mocked. Port the assertions from catalog-service.test.ts:137-163 there first (options-with-addons on both the bare and /services-prefixed paths returns non-404), since that is a live protected-client contract. Then move the two ts-node scripts to scripts/smoke/ so their exclusion from jest is explicit rather than a config line nobody reads.

findings.title: No test enforces auth coverage across the route surface — 65 routes register without verifyAuth, 35 of them on the technician router
findings.evidence: I wrote a scanner that resolves middleware-array spreads (`...adminOnly`) and router.use() so it does not false-positive on the admin routers, and ran it over src/routes. Result: additional.routes.ts 6, auth.route.ts 10 (all legitimate pre-auth endpoints), customerReview.routes.ts 2, payment.routes.ts 1 (the PayMongo webhook, correctly signature-verified instead), pricing.routes.ts 1, service.route.ts 10, technician.routes.ts 35. The technician set includes src/routes/technician.routes.ts:18-19 (`/workers/role/:role`, `/workers/all` → src/services/technicianService.ts:19 and :809-813 `SELECT uid, email, first_name, last_name, phone_number, role`, a bulk PII dump for whole user classes) and :57 (`/workers/:uid/requirements`, compliance documents). These are the LEAK pass's territory, not mine — my finding is that the TEST suite has no mechanism that would ever surface them: tests/anonymous-bypass.test.ts:52-61 comes closest but only checks for the string `verifyAuthOptional`, so a route with NO middleware at all passes it cleanly. Note additional.routes.ts:11-16 carries the comment `// Customer/worker lifecycle — unprotected (mobile calls these without a token)` — verbatim the premise bd8c355 proved false for the other three routes, on endpoints including `POST /additional/:id/payment`. It has no test coverage (`grep -rln additional tests/` matches only admin-communication.test.js, unrelated).
findings.recommendation: Add tests/route-auth-inventory.test.ts: parse every file in src/routes, resolve spread aliases and router.use(), and snapshot the list of routes lacking verifyAuth against an explicit ALLOWED_UNAUTHENTICATED array with a one-line justification per entry. New unauthenticated routes then fail the build until someone writes down why. Seed the allow-list with the current 65 so it is non-blocking on day one, and let the LEAK pass drain technician.routes.ts and additional.routes.ts from it.

findings.title: The column-does-not-exist defect class hit twice this session; the check that would catch it exists but is scoped to one alias in one function
findings.evidence: Two of the nine commits fix the same defect: 880d5bc (bookingService.getBookingsByUserId referenced `gc.phone_number`, a column guest_customers does not have — tests/guest-booking-link.test.ts:4-13) and 799b6aa (scheduler.ts and adminFinanceService selected `payments.updated_at`, which was never created, so the PayMongo retry job raised Postgres 42703 on every run and no failed payment was ever retried — tests/payments-updated-at.test.ts:3-10). Both were found by eye, in production logs, not by a test — payments-updated-at.test.ts:9-10 says so directly: "It surfaced in production pm2 logs during an unrelated Firebase key rotation — nothing was watching for it." The right check was then written, but only for the one case: tests/guest-booking-link.test.ts:50-66 extracts `gc.<col>` references from a single function and cross-checks them against the DDL in adminCreateBookingService.ts/adminGuestService.ts. It generalizes to nothing. The schema is bootstrapped in code, not migrations — `grep -rn 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS' src/` finds 20+ definitions across adminBookingService.ts, adminFinanceService.ts, adminGuestService.ts, adminCreateBookingService.ts, chat.repository.ts and others — so a machine-readable table→column map is fully derivable from src/.
findings.recommendation: New tests/sql-column-contract.test.ts: build a table→columns map by parsing every `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ${...}.<table> (...)` and `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS <col>` in src/, then scan every template-literal SQL string in src/services and src/controllers, resolve `FROM <table> <alias>` / `JOIN <table> <alias>` bindings, and assert each `<alias>.<col>` reference resolves. Start it in report-only mode against a known-offenders allow-list so the existing surface does not block the build, then drive that list to zero. This one test retroactively catches both bugs and is the single highest-leverage addition in this pass after the CI step.

findings.title: ServanaClient has zero tests for the /workers/:uid contract that 65b4337 reshaped, and the backend test's claim about the client's field list is incomplete
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'workers/' test/` in servana_client-main returns nothing — no client test references any /workers endpoint. The two live consumers are servana_client-main/lib/modules/bookings/presentation/screens/booking_detail_screen.dart:284-301 and lib/common/services/assignment_polling_service.dart:125-140. servana_api-main/tests/provider-profile-projection.test.ts:44-52 claims to pin "the fields booking_detail_screen.dart and assignment_polling_service.dart read" and lists firstName, lastName, phoneNumber, photoUrl. The screen actually reads a four-step fallback chain — `firstName`+`lastName` → `w['name']` → `w['email']` → literal 'Technician' (booking_detail_screen.dart:291-296) — and the test names neither `name` nor `email`. I verified there is no functional break: providerProfileProjection.ts:36 includes `name` in PUBLIC_FIELDS, and `email` (WITHHELD_FROM_OTHERS:84) is only the third fallback, so a customer degrades to 'Technician' rather than crashing. But the test reads as a cross-repo contract test and is not one — its field list was written from the fix's intent, not from the client source, so it would not have caught the omission of `name` from PUBLIC_FIELDS, which WOULD have been a visible regression.
findings.recommendation: Two changes. In servana_api-main/tests/provider-profile-projection.test.ts:44-52, add `name` and `email` to the asserted contract explicitly — `name` present, `email` absent — and cite the exact client line for each. In servana_client-main, add test/modules/bookings/worker_profile_parse_test.dart feeding _loadWorkerProfile's parsing the exact projected payload the backend now returns (uid, firstName, lastName, name, phoneNumber, photoUrl, roleName, services) and asserting name and phone resolve and nothing throws on the absent keys.

findings.title: guard-protected-contracts checks route prefixes, not the specific routes ServanaClient calls — and never runs
findings.evidence: servana_api-main/scripts/guard-protected-contracts.mjs:53-56 defines the worker contract as two regexes: `/['\"`]\/worker\//` and `/['\"`]\/workers\//` — the existence of ANY route under those prefixes satisfies it. Running it: all 10 checks pass, exit 0. Meanwhile src/routes/technician.routes.ts:10-15 and docs/WORKER_ROUTE_MIGRATION.md schedule the deletion of 36 legacy /workers routes once telemetry reaches zero. servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:351 still calls `/api/workers/location/$uid` (consumed at lib/modules/tracking/data/tracking_data_source.dart:33, the live customer tracking screen) and :339 still calls `/api/workers/role/$role` — the authenticated successor at src/routes/provider.routes.ts:178 exists but the client has not migrated. Deleting those two routes would break the customer app and the guard would still exit 0, because /workers/available and others remain. Compounding it, the guard is not wired into CI at all (see the deploy.yml finding) — it only runs if a human types `npm run guard:protected-contracts`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the two prefix regexes at scripts/guard-protected-contracts.mjs:53-56 with the explicit route list ServanaClient and ServanaWorker actually call, extracted from servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart and ServanaWorker/lib/core/api/servana_api.dart:310-355 — at minimum /workers/role/:role, /workers/:uid, /workers/location/:uid, /workers/location, /workers/:workerId/job-cards, /workers/bookings/:bookingId/{accept,start,complete,decline}. Then add the guard step to deploy.yml so the check is enforced rather than advisory.

findings.title: ServanaClient's six skipped tests defer to an integration_test/ directory that does not exist, and they cover exactly the token lifecycle this session made load-bearing
findings.evidence: `flutter test` in servana_client-main @ 4868aca reports `+983 ~6` — six skipped. All six are in test/bloc/authentication_bloc_test.dart at :123, :139, :168, :283, :317, :602, each with a skip reason pointing elsewhere: `'Requires flutter_secure_storage platform channel — use integration_test'` (:123-124, :139-140) and `'Full happy path requires injectable FirebaseAuth + ServanaApiClient — use integration_test'` (:283-284). `ls integration_test/` → "No such file or directory". The deferral target has never been created, so these are not deferred, they are dropped. What they cover matters more now than when they were written: bd8c355 and 52667b3 turned six customer routes from optional-auth into hard 401s, and servana_client-main/lib/common/data/backend/servana_api_client.dart:37-46 shows `_headers()` returns `{'Content-Type': 'application/json'}` with NO Authorization header whenever `SessionService.getSession()?.token` is null or empty. Every code path that could produce that state — logout, cold-start before session hydration, expired-token refresh — is in the skipped set. A gap that previously degraded to "served anonymously" now degrades to a 401 and an `onUnauthorized` redirect (:53).
findings.recommendation: Either create integration_test/ and port the six cases, or — cheaper and sufficient for the risk introduced this session — add test/common/data/backend/api_client_headers_test.dart faking SessionService and asserting: a populated token yields the Authorization header; a null session and an empty-string token both yield NO Authorization header (documenting the state that now 401s); and a 401 response invokes onUnauthorized exactly once. Four tests, no platform channel required.

findings.title: No test covers the §21 safe-error boundary, and several hardened controllers return raw exception text
findings.evidence: tests/booking-access.test.ts:167-181 is the suite's only §21 coverage, and it is scoped to BookingAccessError's own message — asserting it contains no 'SELECT', 'servana.', 'bookings', 'user_credentials', 'pg' and does not name the booking's owner. That is good, and it stops at the error class. The handlers wrapping it do not maintain the property: src/controllers/bookingController.ts:51 (createBooking) returns `res.status(400).json({ success: false, message: e.message })`, and src/controllers/paymentController.ts:25 (gcashSubmit) does the same after `if (sendBookingAccessError(res, e)) return` — so any non-BookingAccessError, including a raw pg error carrying a constraint name or column text, is forwarded verbatim to the customer app. src/controllers/technicianController.ts:97-98 does likewise with `error.message || "Failed to fetch worker"`. Nothing tests this.
findings.recommendation: Add a describe to tests/booking-access.test.ts, or fold into the tests/booking-scoped-handlers.test.ts proposed above: for each hardened handler, make the mocked service reject with a realistic pg error (`error: column \"foo\" does not exist` with `code: '42703'`) and assert the response body contains neither the driver text nor the code — only a safe domain message. This is the same shape as the BookingAccessError test at :167-181, applied one layer out where the leak actually is.

findings.title: Coverage shape of the nine new suites: strong where the fix is a pure function, thin where it is a wiring decision
findings.evidence: The 1064 added test lines across nine files (git diff --stat 870fd28..799b6aa) split cleanly. Behavioural unit tests over extracted pure functions — tests/booking-access.test.ts (the access predicate), tests/provider-location-access.test.ts (both new controllers), tests/payment-settlement-access.test.ts (both settlement handlers), tests/legacy-route-telemetry.test.ts, tests/provider-profile-projection.test.ts (the projector) — are genuinely good: they test negatives, ordering, and fail-closed behaviour, not just happy paths. Source-regex assertions — tests/anonymous-bypass.test.ts, tests/guest-booking-link.test.ts, tests/payments-updated-at.test.ts, and the leak-isolation.test.js additions — are the weaker half by necessity (no DB, no server in CI), and they share a failure mode: they assert that a string appears in a file, so they pass when the string appears in a comment (demonstrated concretely by leak-isolation.test.js:124 against booking.routes.ts:14) and they cannot detect middleware ordering, a route registered before a guard, or a guard that runs after the data access it protects. The pattern across all nine: whatever the fix extracted into a testable function is well covered; whatever stayed as a decision inside a controller or a route file is covered by regex or not at all. That is why every P1 above lands on a wiring point — resolveProviderAudience, verifyAuth, the five unguarded call sites, createBooking's identity assignment.
findings.recommendation: No action on its own; this is the through-line explaining the six findings above. The structural remedy is the supertest harness proposed in the jest-exclusion finding: one mounted app with firebase-admin and pg mocked converts the whole source-regex tier into behavioural tests and closes the comment-satisfies-assertion class permanently.
